mechanics.summary: A travel-map hex is 10 kilometers across.

outcome.value: 1 hex = 10 km

exceptions: City maps use 1-kilometer hexes counted as 10-kilometer hexes for speed and encounter frequency.

mechanics.summary: A day has morning, day, evening, and night shifts of roughly six hours; each group member selects one main task each shift unless stated otherwise.

outcome.value: one task per character per shift unless stated otherwise

exceptions: Some tasks allow multiple characters; others require a single character.

mechanics.summary: Travel terrain table defines speed, Driving, Foraging, Hunting, Scrounging, and encounter distance.

lakeRiver.speed: x1 requires boat or amphibious vehicle

exceptions: Speed applies only to off-road driving; marching and on-road driving always use x1.

mechanics.summary: At each shift start roll D6: 1 shifts weather one step toward rain, 6 shifts it one step toward fair.
exceptions: Heavy rain or snow lasts one shift then automatically shifts to cloudy.

mechanics.summary: Weather rules define visibility and heavy-rain/snow travel effects.
Marching on road or open terrain moves 2 hexes per shift; off-road in other terrain moves 1 hex per shift.
In heavy rain each marching PC rolls STAMINA; failure reduces that PC’s base movement by 1 hex for the shift.

outcome.value: failed roll reduces base movement 1 hex

exceptions: Group decides whether to leave stragglers or wait.

mechanics.summary: Off-road marching at night requires one group SURVIVAL roll; failure prevents travel progress that shift.

outcome.value: failed roll causes zero travel progress

mechanics.summary: A third marching shift in one day requires each marcher to roll STAMINA; failure forces rest or sleep instead.

outcome.value: failed marcher cannot march this shift

exceptions: This is in addition to heavy-rain Stamina roll.

mechanics.summary: A fourth marching shift requires another STAMINA roll at -2 and automatically causes sleep deprivation.
exceptions: Failure forces rest or sleep.

mechanics.summary: Entering an off-road hex with no road requires one group SURVIVAL roll; failure enters adjacent right target hex on even die or adjacent left on odd die.
exceptions: Maps and compasses give bonuses.

mechanics.summary: Off-road terrain speed x1/2 costs 2 movement to enter, x1/3 costs 3, and movement can accumulate across shifts; on-road terrain has no effect.

outcome.value: entry movement cost is inverse speed factor

mechanics.summary: Night driving halves effective travel speed on and off road, rounding fractions up.

outcome.value: ceil(travel speed / 2)

mechanics.summary: At each driving shift start make terrain-modified DRIVING roll; entering a new off-road terrain requires another roll, heavy rain adds -2, and failure rolls a mishap.
trigger: driving shift begins or new off-road terrain entered

outcome.value: failed roll uses Driving Mishaps table

exceptions: Referee determines mishap hex, typically halfway through shift.

mechanics.summary: Driving-mishap 2D6 table defines outcomes.

value.3: roadkill: kill random hunting-table animal; vehicle-front damage ceil(half animal hit capacity)
value.4: busted gearbox: no further movement; Tech plus vehicle spare part, one attempt/shift
value.5: dirty fuel: drain tank and refuel
value.6: bogged down: no further movement; Stamina or other-vehicle help, one attempt/shift
value.8: roadblock: choose other hex or Stamina one shift to remove obstacle
value.9: engine overheated: stop rest of shift
value.10: blown tire/thrown track: no movement; Tech +2 plus vehicle spare part, one attempt/shift
value.11: crash: front damage equals travel speed

mechanics.summary: Vehicle fuel consumption is listed liters per hex and doubles off-road; idling uses listed consumption per shift rather than per hex.

outcome.value: listed liters per hex, doubled off-road; listed liters per idling shift

mechanics.summary: Converting an engine to alcohol fuel needs TECH and one shift; alcohol fuel doubles vehicle consumption.
trigger: engine converted to alcohol fuel or uses alcohol fuel

outcome.value: alcohol consumption x2

mechanics.summary: One encumbrance unit of raw material produces one liter alcohol fuel; still production requires stationary shift use monitored by at least one person.

outcome.value: 1 raw-material unit per liter

exceptions: A person gathers 30 raw-material encumbrance units per field-work shift, halved in winter.

mechanics.summary: A horse carries rider plus 25 extra encumbrance units or a second person; when led it carries 50 units; it needs one rest shift daily.
Riding a horse a third shift needs MOBILITY modified by Rider talent; failure makes horse lame and incapacitated.
trigger: horse ridden third shift in day

outcome.value: failed roll makes horse incapacitated

mechanics.summary: One lookout may watch and march; at encounter approach they make a passive unpushable RECON roll, opposed only against ambush.

outcome.value: success spots group first; failure means encountered group spots first

exceptions: Without lookout, group cannot spot threats before they are upon them.

unknowns: Encounter approach and ambush are Referee-managed.

mechanics.summary: Lookout has -2 when group motorized and encountered group on foot, automatic failure if all inside closed armored vehicle, and +2 when group on foot and encountered group motorized.
exceptions: If both groups are in vehicles, roll normally.

mechanics.summary: Backing off unseen from an encounter costs one additional off-road hex of movement modified by terrain.
trigger: group backs off without being spotted

outcome.value: spend 1 additional off-road hex movement modified by terrain

mechanics.summary: One character per hex per shift rolls terrain-modified SURVIVAL; each success gives one D100 scrap-table roll, and repeated same-hex scrounging has cumulative -1.

outcome.value: one scrap D100 roll per success

exceptions: Helpers allowed.
Scavenging finds takes a separate full shift.
Referee can choose or reroll finds.

mechanics.summary: A Referee-allowed quick search needs no roll, gives one free scrap-table roll, does not count as scrounging, and allows another main-shift task.

outcome.value: one free scrap-table roll

exceptions: Only in likely-scrap areas.

mechanics.summary: One character per hex per shift chooses food or water then rolls terrain- and season-modified SURVIVAL; food success yields wild-food rations per success and water success fills water bottles.

outcome.value: food rations equal successes or fill water bottles

exceptions: Helpers allowed.
Repeated same-hex foraging has cumulative -1 reset after a week except winter.

mechanics.summary: Foraging seasonal modifiers are spring -1, summer 0, autumn +1, winter -2.
Terrain-modified SURVIVAL success tracks prey; roll hunting table once per success and choose one prey to hunt.

outcome.value: one prey-table roll per success

exceptions: Only one hunter per hex per shift; helpers allowed; repeated same-hex hunting has cumulative -1 reset after week.

mechanics.summary: To hunt tracked prey, make straight RECON to approach without alerting it, then ranged attack; damage at least animal hit capacity or a critical hit kills it, otherwise it escapes.

outcome.value: kill prey or it escapes

exceptions: Approach modifier depends on chosen range.
Usually one shot.
Raw meat requires Stamina against food poisoning.

mechanics.summary: For trappable prey, after tracking it make another SURVIVAL roll; success catches it without shooting.

outcome.value: prey caught

mechanics.summary: Hunting D6 table defines prey hit capacity, trapping, and cooked-food yield.

value.1: grouse; capacity 1; no trap; 1 ration; shotgun required

mechanics.summary: One character per hex per shift adjacent to water, or from moving boat, uses fishing gear and SURVIVAL; success yields cooked-food rations equal to successes.

outcome.value: food rations equal successes

exceptions: Helpers allowed; repeated same-hex fishing has cumulative -1 reset after a day.
Raw fish requires Stamina against food poisoning.

mechanics.summary: Grenade fishing needs no skill roll and yields D6 food rations; it cannot be used more than once per hex per shift.

outcome.value: D6 food rations

exceptions: One use per hex per shift.

mechanics.summary: Making camp takes one shift; one character rolls SURVIVAL with helpers allowed. Success gives sheltered rest and cover; failure still camps but causes hidden camp-mishap roll.

outcome.value: success makes sheltered camp; failure uses camp mishap

exceptions: Referee may trigger applicable mishap anytime at camp.

mechanics.summary: After making camp, RECON result can hide it; test that recorded result as opposed roll against passing enemies. Without it, enemies within visual range automatically spot camp.

outcome.value: record Recon result for opposed detection

mechanics.summary: Sleeping one shift without fire or other heat requires STAMINA against hypothermia, except on warm summer nights.
trigger: group sleeps at camp without heat

outcome.value: avoid hypothermia

exceptions: Fire smoke reveals position within visual range.

unknowns: Warm summer night requires Referee input.

mechanics.summary: Cooking wild meat, fish, or vegetables needs campfire or kitchen; a campfire cooks up to 12 daily rations in a shift, and failed SURVIVAL makes eaters roll Stamina against food poisoning.

outcome.value: wild food becomes domestic food

exceptions: Cooking can occur in same shift as another character makes camp.
Success or failure both convert food.

mechanics.summary: Camp-mishap D10 table defines failed-camp outcomes.

value.2: flooding: Stamina against hypothermia; no sleep
value.3: fire dies: Stamina against hypothermia except warm weather
value.4: fire: tent destroyed; intensity-D fire; Mobility failure loses Referee-chosen gear
value.6: lice: 1 stress daily and cannot sleep until Medical Aid succeeds
value.7: mosquitoes: roll 2D6 base dice; 1 stress per success
value.10: Referee-selected random character gear breaks; Tech repair

exceptions: Reroll inapplicable mishap.

mechanics.summary: A dramatic interruption such as combat means a shift no longer counts as rest.
trigger: rest shift interrupted by dramatic activity

outcome.value: do not count shift as rest

mechanics.summary: A dramatic interruption such as combat means a shift no longer counts as sleep.
trigger: sleep shift interrupted by dramatic activity

outcome.value: do not count shift as sleep

mechanics.summary: Without camp, every group member rolls SURVIVAL to find sleeping spot; failure gives no sleep and all suffer cold effects.

outcome.value: failure means no sleep and cold exposure

mechanics.summary: A character exploring for more than half a shift cannot rest or sleep in that shift.
trigger: exploration occupies more than half shift

outcome.value: rest and sleep unavailable that shift

mechanics.summary: Water travel follows land-driving procedure; boat passengers may rest or sleep unless keeping watch, fishing, or doing another task.

outcome.value: rest or sleep while passenger

exceptions: Not while keeping watch, fishing, or another action.

referenceData.notes: Individual D100 result rows are pure inventory reference data except when an item’s printed effect is extracted in its gear batch.
Table is consumed by the printed light/darkness procedures.
